title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page (p.1) sets up the infinitesimal construction of the Gauss–Manin connection. T_0 = V(I) ⊂ T is a square-zero thickening. X', X'' are two smooth liftings over T of a smooth X_0/T_0. P is the sheaf on X_0 of local T-isomorphisms X'→X'' lifting the identity. P is a right torsor under G = Hom(Ω^1_{X_0/T_0}, f_0^*I) = T_{X_0/T_0} ⊗ I. Each local isomorphism p gives a chain map u(p): Ω·_{X'/T} → Ω·_{X''/T}. Each g ∈ G acts by v(g), and v(g) − id = d k(g) + k(g) d, where k(g) is contraction with the I-valued derivation g (Cartan homotopy formula). The local maps u(p) need not glue, since P may have no global section. The goal is a canonical morphism Ω·_{X'/T} → Ω·_{X''/T} in the derived category. Applying RΓ (or Rf_*) then gives the canonical identification of the de Rham cohomologies of the two liftings, which is the source of the Gauss–Manin connection (crystalline philosophy).

This page abstracts the situation. Data:
- X is a ringed space, K', K'' are complexes of O_X-modules, G is an abelian sheaf, P is a right G-torsor.
- u: P → Hom^0(K',K'') takes values in chain maps.
- v: G → (degree-0 Hom) is additive.
- h: G → Hom^{-1}(K',K'') supplies homotopies, with v(g) = d h(g) + h(g) d.
- Compatibility: u(pg) = u(p) ∘or+ v(g).
The goal: produce a morphism K' → K'' in D(X), hence RΓ_X(K') → RΓ_X(K''), compatible with the Γ(O_X)-structure and later relativised over X → T.

The device has three steps.
1. Encode P as an extension 0 → G → Ḡ → Z → 0 with g^{-1}(1) ≅ P. This is the standard dictionary H^1(X,G) = Ext^1(Z,G) between torsors and extensions of Z by G.
2. Form the two-term complex L = [G → Ḡ]. It is quasi-isomorphic to Z[0] provided G sits in degree −1 and Ḡ in degree 0. The page labels them L^0, L^1; the next page silently corrects this to −1, 0.
3. On the next page, a strict chain map φ: L → H = Hom·(K',K'') is built with φ^{-1} = h and φ^0|_P = u. This uses the universal property: a homomorphism Ḡ → F is the same as a homomorphism w: G → F plus a map P → F satisfying u(p+g) = u(p) + w(g). Here w = δh.

The result is Z ≅ L → H in D(Ab(X)). Tensoring with O_X gives O_X → H → RHom(K',K''). Applying RΓ^0 gives an element of Hom_D(K',K''), a canonical global derived morphism glued from local chain maps.

In short: local chain maps related by strictly additive homotopies, indexed by an abelian torsor, glue to a derived-category morphism. The obstruction to an honest global chain map is the class of P in H^1(X,G), killed by the homotopies.
errors: As written, u(pg) = u(p)v(g) is multiplicative (composition), with v valued in endomorphisms of K''. But h is declared G → Hom^{-1}(K',K'') and the next page's universal property of Ḡ needs the additive form u(pg) = u(p) + v(g) with v = dh+hd in Hom^0(K',K''). The abstract axioms are type-inconsistent on this page.

Passing from de Rham to the abstract setting tacitly uses the following fact: h(g) := u(p)∘k(g) is independent of p, and v(g) − 1 = u(p)^{-1}(u(pg) − u(p)) is additive in g. Both hold only because I^2 = 0, so changing p alters u(p)k(g) by terms in I^2. This hypothesis is not stated.
L is labelled with degrees 0,1 (L^0 = G, L^1 = Ḡ). With that grading, L is quasi-isomorphic to Z[−1], not Z. The correct grading −1, 0 is used on the next page.

The step H = Hom·(K',K'') → RHom(K',K'') (next page) is a map, not an isomorphism, unless K' is K-flat/projective or K'' is K-injective. Only the map is needed, so this is fine. The 'tensoring with O_X' step is superfluous: Z → H already gives a class in H^0 RHom = Hom_D.

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism between de Rham complexes of two infinitesimal liftings, glued from local isomorphisms via Cartan-homotopy contractions, giving the Gauss–Manin connection.
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline/infinitesimal construction of the Gauss–Manin connection (crystalline nature of de Rham cohomology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, 1966/68); Katz–Oda 1968; Berthelot 1974
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968)

ideas.what: Identify a G-torsor P with an extension 0→G→Ḡ→Z→0 with fibre over 1 equal to P.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Tôhoku / SGA 7, SGA 4 XVIII with Deligne)
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I exp. VII (biextensions/torsors); Giraud 'Cohomologie non abélienne'

ideas.what: Glue local chain maps indexed by a torsor, with additive homotopies, into a derived morphism via a strict map [G→Ḡ] → Hom·(K',K'') from a resolution of Z.
ideas.modern_name: Descent of morphisms in the derived category / homotopy-coherent gluing in degree ≤1 (truncated Čech/torsor descent)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (cf. Illusie's treatment of deformations and torsors, Complexe cotangent 1971–72)

missed.claim: This is a clean, Čech-free abstract lemma: a G-torsor of local chain maps K'→K'', related by strictly additive homotopies, yields a canonical morphism in D(X). It is obtained by mapping the two-term resolution [G→Ḡ] of Z into Hom·. This is an elegant packaging of the Katz–Oda/crystalline gluing, but it is a known technique and adds no new mathematics.
missed.quote: On introduit l'extension Ḡ de Z par G ... g^{-1}(1) ≃ P ... soit L le complexe ... G → Ḡ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Pedagogical value only. It is a degree-1 instance of homotopy-coherent descent that the ∞-categorical literature now handles routinely.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful working notes reconstructing the canonical connection via a neat torsor-extension trick. The mathematics (crystalline Gauss–Manin, torsors as extensions of Z) is standard and published by Grothendieck, Katz–Oda and Berthelot.
transcription_corrections: 'u(g) = dh(g) + h(g)d' should read 'v(g) = d h(g) + h(g) d' (cf. previous page v(g)−id = dk+kd).
'On veut une application [?] un homomorphisme' reads roughly 'On veut associer un homom. dans la cat. dérivée K' → K'' d'où ...'.
The target of v appears to be Hom·(K', K'') (second argument K''); the first argument is ambiguous in the image.
'(cas [?] connu de G-torseurs ...)' is likely '(cas connu des G-torseurs ...)'.
Superscripts in the last display are L^0 over G and L^1 over Ḡ, written above the terms, not as labels of separate rows.
